_description: Task13 DRIFT field, COARSE transcription -- the 0.4mm far-field grid. The fine sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_fine.json) is the 0.1mm near-field and final grid. PAD/GAP SPLIT: this file uses pixelSize 3.6 / pixelGap 0.8 while the fine file uses 3.5 / 0.9. That is NOT a typo -- both are the same 4.4mm pitch, and each file uses the split that divides its OWN spacing exactly: 3.6/0.4=9 and 0.8/0.4=2 here, versus 3.5/0.1=35 and 0.9/0.1=9 there. The fine split cannot be used at the coarse spacing (3.5/0.4=8.75), which is the whole reason there are two files. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = GridPotential - BulkField * (z_cathode - z_grid), where z_grid = pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition + PcbWidth = 10.0 + 1.6 = 11.6mm, z_cathode = driftZDepth rounded up to a whole coarse cell = 159.9 -> 160.0mm, so the bulk is 148.4mm. At 50 V/mm that gives -2500 - 50*148.4 = -9920 V. This file currently holds CathodePotential -7500, i.e. 33.69 V/mm. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one.
